spans.s:
duḥkha
(‘suffering’)
------------------------------------------
All living beings seriously try to escape from दुःख or sorrow and suffering. An analysis of the causes of दुःख and the means of getting relief from it often find a place in philosophical systems.
Duḥkha has been defined in various ways by these systems. Some of them are: that which is characterised by pain; One of the qualities or states of मिन्द् that can be known by the reactions seen on the face; that which brings about hatred and so on.
Duḥkha can be brought about by various factors such as: loss of freedom; mental tensions and diseases; sickness of the body; loss of honour; enemies; unhappy मर्रिअगे; living in a bad place; serving a bad master; old-age; living in the houses of others, depending upon them and so on.
Duḥkha has been classified in various ways by different systems. Here, the causes are given greater importance. For instance—those caused by: diseases, the six enemies such as lust and greed, tendencies carried over from previous lives, birth and death.
Persons easily susceptible to jealousy, hatred, cruelty and a doubting nature are always subjected to दुःख.
Though appropriate remedial measures are available for these duḥkhas, मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन् from transmigratory existence is the ultimate and the surest remedy.
